_meta.description: Frozen final configuration for the GDX next-day-direction strategy, selected entirely from the in-sample process (train+validation). This file is the single source of truth for the parameters to apply in any holdout evaluation.
_meta.frozen_from: results/backtest_results.csv (rank 1 of 5, the only config profitable after costs)
selection_process: results/walk_forward_grid.csv: walk-forward grid search over lookback x threshold, ranked by walk-forward Sharpe
results/backtest_results.csv: top 5 walk-forward configs re-run through the realistic-cost backtest engine (src/backtest.py); this config was rank 1 and the only one profitable after costs
results/robustness_report.md: perturbation, sub-period, and cost-sensitivity checks on this exact config
results/significance_report.md: t-test and bootstrap significance checks on this exact config
_meta.DO_NOT: Do not modify this file's parameter values and do not re-run any tuning, grid search, or parameter selection after this point. This file freezes the in-sample decision; any change here would leak holdout-era judgment back into a supposedly-frozen in-sample choice.

signal.description: signal[t] = -sign(GDX[t]/GDX[t-20] - 1) if |GDX[t]/GDX[t-20] - 1| >= 0.02 else 0 (flat deadzone). direction_sign=-1 is fixed for the whole backtest period, not adaptively refit (unlike results/walk_forward_grid.csv's adaptive quarterly direction, which this frozen config does NOT use).

exit_rule.description: Fixed 1-day hold. n_days=0 in src.backtest.exit_after_n_days reproduces the original results/timing_spec.md convention exactly: signal known at close t, entry executes at close t+1, exit executes at close t+2.

timing.entry: market-on-close, at close t+1 (t = signal date)

position_sizing.note: position_fraction and allow_fractional_shares are the strategy's sizing rule and should carry over to any account size; account_size_used_for_in_sample_eval was only the reference size used for in-sample reporting, not a constraint on deployment size.

cost_assumptions.description: $0.005/share commission + 0.05% (5bps) slippage per leg (entry and exit each), applied unfavorably to the execution price. See src/backtest.py and results/backtest_results.csv.

known_limitations: Mean daily strategy return is NOT statistically distinguishable from zero (t-test p=0.578, results/significance_report.md).
Bootstrap 90% interval for trade-level Sharpe is [-0.33, 0.64] -- straddles zero; the positive point-estimate Sharpe is not resampling-stable.
Only 2 of 4 equal chronological sub-periods were profitable in-sample; performance was concentrated in 2006-2009 and 2015-2018 (results/robustness_report.md).
Only 2 of 9 nearby (lookback, threshold) parameter combinations (+/-20% perturbation) were profitable -- a narrow, fragile optimum, not a broad edge.
Doubling assumed costs flips CAGR from +0.44% to -13.8%.

This config was fixed-direction (reversal) for its entire in-sample backtest; the walk-forward grid's more optimistic Sharpe (0.379) was earned under an adaptive, quarterly-refit direction that this frozen config does not use.

None of this constitutes a validated trading edge. Freezing these parameters preserves methodological discipline (no further in-sample tuning) -- it is not a claim that the strategy is expected to be profitable out of sample.
